title: Brett Lee Names Former KKR Teammate Jacques Kallis as Greatest Cricketer of All Time
excerpt: The Australian fast bowler picks the South African all-rounder over Sachin Tendulkar and Ricky Ponting, citing their years together at Kolkata Knight Riders.
body:
• Brett Lee has named former KKR teammate Jacques Kallis as the greatest cricketer of all time, placing him above Sachin Tendulkar and Ricky Ponting
  • Lee rates Tendulkar as the best pure batsman but calls Kallis the most complete cricketer for his batting, bowling, and fielding across formats
  • The two played together at Kolkata Knight Riders, where Lee witnessed Kallis's dominance firsthand during IPL seasons
  • Kallis retired with 13,289 Test runs, 45 centuries, and 292 wickets — the only player to score 10,000 runs and take 250 wickets in both Tests and ODIs

Lee's Pick Skips Cricket Royalty

Former Australian fast bowler Brett Lee has named South African all-rounder Jacques Kallis as the greatest cricketer of all time — a choice that bypasses legends like Sachin Tendulkar, Ricky Ponting, and Brian Lara.

Speaking on his YouTube channel Brett Lee TV and in a separate conversation with former Pakistan speedster Shoaib Akhtar, Lee was unequivocal in his pick.

"I loved playing against fast bowlers. Jacques Kallis is the best all-rounder, no question. He is the best cricketer ever."

— Brett Lee

The declaration is notable because Lee does not slight Tendulkar in the process. He calls the Indian maestro the greatest batsman he ever bowled to, ahead of Brian Lara. But when it comes to the most complete cricketer — someone who could bat, bowl, and field at the highest level simultaneously — Lee says the answer is Kallis, full stop.

The KKR Connection

Lee and Kallis were teammates at Kolkata Knight Riders during the Indian Premier League, giving the Australian a front-row seat to the South African's abilities. Lee served as both player and bowling mentor for KKR, while Kallis was a cornerstone of the franchise's batting and bowling lineup. Kallis played a crucial role in KKR's maiden IPL title in 2012, scoring 407 runs and taking 15 wickets across the tournament.

In a revealing anecdote from their time together at KKR, Lee described how every bowler in the squad failed to beat Kallis during a net session.

"I have got arguably the greatest cricketer Jacques Kallis playing for KKR, batting at one end, and we are bowling at the centre wicket," Lee recalled on Brett Lee TV. "I am trying really hard to get Kallis out but this guy is going bang bang. I could not get Jacques Kallis out. All our bowlers were struggling with a brand new ball on a brand new wicket, and Kallis was making it look so easy."

It took KKR bowling coach Wasim Akram — widely regarded as the greatest left-arm fast bowler in cricket history — to finally dismiss Kallis. After watching the South African dispatch delivery after delivery with ease, Akram stepped in wearing sand shoes instead of spikes. He set Kallis up with a series of inswingers before turning one away off the seam to find the edge.

"As he walked back, he winked at me and said 'watch this!'" Lee recalled. "He turned the ball over, took one away straight. Nick and gone! And I said, 'Mate! You are a genius.'"

Numbers That Back the Claim

Kallis's career statistics make a compelling case for Lee's assessment. The right-hander played 166 Tests for South Africa from 1995 to 2014, scoring 13,289 runs with 45 centuries and taking 292 wickets. In 328 ODIs, he accumulated 11,579 runs with 17 centuries and claimed 273 wickets. He also took 200 Test catches, primarily at slip.

He remains the only player in cricket history to have scored more than 10,000 runs and taken more than 250 wickets in both Test and ODI cricket. Former India captain Sourav Ganguly once called Kallis "the most effective player" in Test cricket after watching him dominate a home series against Sri Lanka in 2012.

Where Tendulkar and Lara Stand

Lee was careful to separate the categories. Tendulkar, he said, was the hardest batsman he ever bowled to.

"I hated bowling to Sachin because he was just so good. Great technique," Lee said in his conversation with Akhtar. "It just looked like he had more time. The best way to explain the meaning of time in cricket is that it felt like Sachin was batting on the return crease — it just felt like he had more time to play against me."

On Lara, Lee acknowledged the West Indian's brilliance: "It did not matter how quick you bowled against him, he could smash you in six different areas on the ground." But Lee ultimately placed Tendulkar ahead of Lara, and Kallis above both — not as a better batsman, but as the more complete cricketer.

An Australian's Bond With Indian Cricket

Lee, who took 310 Test wickets and 380 ODI wickets for Australia, has maintained deep ties with Indian cricket. Beyond his IPL stint at KKR, Lee received a letter of appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and has described his time in India as "brilliant." His consistent championing of Kallis — a player perhaps underappreciated relative to flashier contemporaries — has resonated with cricket fans across the subcontinent who appreciate the all-round game.

The debate over cricket's greatest will never be settled. But for one of the fastest bowlers to ever play the game, the answer was never really in doubt.
